findings.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when caller only has VIEW scope on all-groups (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), letting view-only admins create groups and pass requireManage() gates; should check MANAGE only, and the GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() Javadoc codifies the same wrong behavior

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() (authz Resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() into hasPermission, so the findByName lookup misses, falls back to all-groups, and the returned set contains Resource IDs rather than group IDs, breaking group-scoped user searches via the UserModel.GROUPS attribute

UsersResource.java: removal of .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) on the search stream means callers with no global view and an empty getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() get the raw unfiltered user stream, potentially exposing all users unless toRepresentation independently filters on canView

GroupPermissionsV2.canView()/canList() only consult the all-groups resource, so an admin with VIEW on a specific group gets 403 from GET /groups (requireList) and the per-group canView filter in GroupsResource.getGroups never runs, making per-group view permissions unusable via the list endpoint

AdminPermissions.java: feature-flag check moved from event time to registration time, so if registerListener runs before Profile is configured or the profile is reconfigured at runtime, the cleanup listener for removed roles/clients/groups is silently never registered, leaving stale permission resources/policies

AdminPermissionsSchema.java: switch on String resourceType throws NullPointerException for null resourceType (previously handled gracefully), and the new default -> throw IllegalStateException changes behavior for unknown types from returning null to an uncaught exception

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest @AfterEach removes scope permissions but not the 'Only My Admin User Policy' user policy created in every test, so subsequent tests attempt to create a duplicate-named policy and conflict or leak state
GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() Javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs' but the method returns a Set<String>
GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManageMembers Javadoc references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers

getGroupsWithViewPermission() and getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) were removed from the public GroupPermissionEvaluator interface with no deprecation cycle, breaking external SPI callers at compile time

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

AdminPermissions.java: feature-flag check moved from event time to registration time, so if registerListener runs before Profile is configured or the profile is reconfigured at runtime, the cleanup listener for removed roles/clients/groups is silently never registered, leaving stale permission resources/policies

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener changes the feature-flag check from being evaluated on every event (inside onEvent) to being evaluated once at registration time (wrapping manager.register). This is a behavioral change, but the proposed finding relies on assumptions not established in the diff: that Profile configuration might not be initialized when registerListener runs, or that Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ can be reconfigured at runtime. The diff alone does not show any such initialization ordering issue or runtime reconfiguration capability, so the claim that the listener will be “silently never registered” in real deployments is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this patch.

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest @AfterEach removes scope permissions but not the 'Only My Admin User Policy' user policy created in every test, so subsequent tests attempt to create a duplicate-named policy and conflict or leak state

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows changes to runtime classes (resources, permission evaluators, schema) and does not include any test class named `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, nor any `@AfterEach` method, nor creation/removal of an "Only My Admin User Policy". Since the claimed duplicate policy/leaked state behavior depends on code not present in the provided diff, the finding is not verifiable from this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() Javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs' but the method returns a Set<String>

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the Javadoc for `GroupPermissionEvaluator#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` states `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` but the method signature is `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission();`. This is a concrete, verifiable documentation/type mismatch introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManageMembers Javadoc references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionEvaluator` the Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says: `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false.` This is a copy/paste error: it should reference `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (the corresponding capability) rather than `canManageMembership`. This mismatch is present in the diff and is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupsWithViewPermission() and getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) were removed from the public GroupPermissionEvaluator interface with no deprecation cycle, breaking external SPI callers at compile time

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes two methods from the public `GroupPermissionEvaluator` interface (`boolean getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group);` and `Set<String> getGroupsWithViewPermission();`) and replaces them with a differently named/signature method `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission();`. This is a source-incompatible change: any code (including external extensions) compiled against the old interface will fail to compile without updates, and there is no deprecation/bridge method shown in the diff.
